prompt: Implement write_text_atomically(path, text, encoding='utf-8') using a temporary file in the same directory and os.replace. Explain why the temporary file should be on the same filesystem.
target:
from pathlib import Path
import os
import tempfile

def write_text_atomically(path, text, encoding='utf-8'):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=f'.{path.name}.')
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding=encoding) as stream:
            stream.write(text)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.replace(temp_name, path)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            os.unlink(temp_name)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        raise

# Same-directory placement makes an atomic rename much more likely/portable.

The temporary file is created beside the destination so replacement stays on the same filesystem; os.replace atomically swaps the name on supported filesystems. This does not guarantee durability of the directory entry after sudden power loss on every platform.
